method: Read-only source review of candidate commits against docs/stabilization/inventory.json EXT-F-1003-T46 and forcing-function-tests. No tests, build, browser, or process was run.

A_runtime_acceptance.verdict: PENDING; no browser execution or runtime evidence reviewed
A_runtime_acceptance.candidate_capability: The runner installs entry and post-probe CDP breakpoints in the spawned profile's service worker script, saves the real port using trusted panel input, then observes the handler and its later availability broadcast.
A_runtime_acceptance.acceptance_blocker: The acceptance does not establish that either pause was caused by this Save. It accepts the first entry and postProbe pauses without comparing observedAt to a Save timestamp; those pauses can predate the input. It also does not require a matching /health request, so the listener is diagnostic context, not proof that the configured port was probed. Entry and postProbe can be drawn from different handler invocations.
A_runtime_acceptance.native_vs_http: Breakpoint-based completion is transport-independent: bootstrap.ts:957 probes and :960 broadcasts after either result, so healthy native-host success need not issue HTTP. The disposable listener can observe HTTP /health, but this runner never asserts that event or records an explicit native/HTTP classification.
A_runtime_acceptance.false_pass_risk: Pre-save or unrelated rediscover invocation(s) can satisfy both pause predicates; separate calls can be paired. Therefore current source can pass without attributable Save-triggered rediscovery.
A_runtime_acceptance.false_fail_risks: Unminified-shape regex and tight breakpoint location assertions may reject a behaviorally correct changed bundle; worker target replacement or debugger attach/resume failures can also fail the runner. These are explicit failures, not acceptance passes.

prior_findings.title: Removed VALID_PORT still used in persistence assertion
prior_findings.evidence: f15e907 replaces that use with observedPort.port in the save/reload path (tests/browser/settings-local-controls-acceptance.mjs:292-308).

prior_findings.title: Probe before next alarm is not attributable to Save rediscovery
prior_findings.evidence: The alarm timing check is replaced by worker breakpoints, but observations remain uncorrelated to Save time or invocation (tests/browser/settings-local-controls-acceptance.mjs:108-115, 288-303).

prior_findings.title: HTTP observer marks working native rediscovery as failure
prior_findings.evidence: Acceptance now watches the worker handler/post-probe broadcast instead of requiring GET /health; the dead-port listener returns 503 and cannot fake native health (tests/browser/settings-local-controls-acceptance.mjs:17-41, 101-151).

additional_findings.title: CDP resume is not awaited before success
additional_findings.evidence: The paused-event listener fires Debugger.resume without awaiting it; waitFor can return as soon as pauses are recorded and assert a still-null resumeError before the promise settles (tests/browser/settings-local-controls-acceptance.mjs:108-115, 296-299). A later resume rejection can be missed.

additional_findings.title: Cleanup is fail-fast and can skip override cleanup
additional_findings.evidence: In finally, watcher.close() and worker.detach() precede the saved-port cleanup without independent try/finally guards (tests/browser/settings-local-controls-acceptance.mjs:322-329). A debugger cleanup error skips clearing the override; outer harness eventually terminates its owned browser/profile (native-sidepanel-qa-harness.mjs:423 onward), while the top-level listener closes in its own finally.

B_quality_verdict.forcing_function_assessment: The test reads real released-worker code and observes real handler statements, a stronger seam than storage or broadcast-only evidence. It still lacks the forcing condition that makes a no-op or unrelated invocation fail: the Save event and matching handler execution need a shared temporal/correlation key, and completion needs to belong to that same invocation. The current listener count is captured but not asserted after Save.

required_next: Correlate one handler entry and its post-probe completion strictly after the trusted Save action (and ensure both belong to the same invocation); await each debugger resume and preserve cleanup even if debugger teardown fails. Then run the guarded native acceptance and obtain fresh independent evidence review.
